name: PyTorch
works_with: Python, with optional NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm or Intel GPU support
short: A Python package for tensor maths on GPUs and building deep neural networks with automatic differentiation.
what: PyTorch gives you tensors like NumPy's with strong GPU acceleration, plus deep neural networks built on a tape-based autograd system. It's split into parts like `torch`, `torch.autograd`, `torch.nn` and `torch.utils` for data loading. The README says people use it as a GPU-powered NumPy replacement or as a deep learning research platform.
who: Anyone writing or training neural networks in Python. Most people should install the prebuilt binaries. Building from source is for contributors or unusual setups, and the README says it needs at least 10 GB of disk and 30 to 60 minutes.
needs: Python (3.10 or later to build from source)
For GPU support: NVIDIA CUDA and cuDNN v9.0 or above, AMD ROCm 4.0 or above on Linux, or Intel's GPU prerequisites
For source builds: a C++20 compiler (gcc 11.3.0 or newer on Linux), or Visual Studio build tools on Windows
For the Docker route: Docker v23.0 or later

steps.title: Get the install command for your machine
steps.text: The README sends you to pytorch.org/get-started/locally for the pip or Conda command that matches your OS and GPU.

steps.title: Or run a prebuilt Docker image
Or build from source: get the code
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch
cd pytorch
# if you are updating an existing checkout
git submodule sync
git submodule update --init --recursive

steps.title: Install the build dependencies
steps.text: Run this from the pytorch folder. Linux and Windows have extra packages listed in the README.

steps.title: Build and install
steps.text: This is the macOS command. On Linux, the README has you set `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` first.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Start with the tutorials at pytorch.org/tutorials, which the README lists first under Getting Started. The examples repo at github.com/pytorch/examples has code across all domains.

watch: A source build needs at least 10 GB of free disk and 30 to 60 minutes the first time.
In Docker, data loaders that use multiple processes need more shared memory than the default. The README says to use `--ipc=host` or `--shm-size`.
The README doesn't list the pip install command itself. It lives on pytorch.org.
